pattern_per_coaching_article.inconsistency_note: Total marks 200 ≠ the '100 marks per paper' also stated in the same source. Do NOT use 200 marks or 2-marks-per-question for any strategy or time guidance until the official notification is read.

content_strategy_note: Build content at Class 9-10 NCERT/PSEB level for Science, Mathematics and Social Science. Punjabi Paper A is the gate exam — prioritise. All lessons should use examIds: ['ett']. Science and SST lessons shared with master examId continue to serve ETT. New ETT-specific Punjabi lessons must be reviewed by a native Gurmukhi speaker before publishing.

topics.title: Gurmukhi Script & Phonology: letters, vowels, consonants, lagaan-maatraan, dutt-akhar
Word Classes & Grammar: noun, pronoun, adjective, verb, adverb; gender, number; prefixes/suffixes
Vocabulary: synonyms, antonyms, one-word substitution, idioms and proverbs, correct spelling
Sentence Types: simple, compound, complex; punctuation; sentence conversion
Punjabi Culture, Folklore, Folk Songs, Folk Arts, Festivals
Punjabi Idioms (ਮੁਹਾਵਰੇ) and Proverbs (ਅਖਾਣ) — 30 key items
Number System: rational/irrational, HCF/LCM, exponents, real numbers
Algebra & Arithmetic: linear equations, ratio/proportion, %, profit/loss, SI/CI, AP
Geometry & Mensuration: lines/angles/triangles, quadrilaterals/circles, area, volume

Paper_B_Science.note: Covered by existing sci-* and science-* lessons with examId ett. Gaps: sound, light (ett-science-light exists), chemical reactions, acids/bases, carbon compounds, human eye.

Paper_B_Social_Studies.note: Partially covered by master+ett SST lessons. ETT-specific framing at Class 6-10 level needed.

topics.title: Punjab Geography: rivers, physical features, climate, soils, crops
Sikh History: Guru period, Banda Singh Bahadur, Maharaja Ranjit Singh
Civics & Economy: Constitution, Parliament, Rights, Indian Economy basics

Paper_B_English.note: Partially covered by eng-grammar lesson. Gaps: unseen passage, tenses, voice, narration.

Paper_B_Hindi.note: Partially covered by hindi-sandhi lesson. Gaps: tadbhav/tatsam, idioms, antonyms.
